02 / THE METHOD

A decision with
a chain of evidence.

The private alpha joins constrained planning, controlled execution, observations, and historical verification. These are tested mechanisms with explicit boundaries.

  1. 01

    Plan a bounded change.

    Declare paths to close and access that must remain.

    Graph planning operates within explicit size and work limits. A partial search can report FEASIBLE or UNKNOWN; the system does not label every answer optimal.

  2. 02

    Separate approval roles.

    Require distinct roles before execution.

    Durable intent, idempotency, and worker leases constrain execution. Two approval roles are enforced; the software alone cannot prove that two different humans hold them.

  3. 03

    Observe the resource.

    Check denial alongside a positive control.

    A failed application is not a successful revocation. Returned access produces RESIDUAL. An inconclusive or unavailable observation produces UNKNOWN.

  4. 04

    Preserve the record.

    Verify history against a supplied trust root.

    Signed historical receipts support offline integrity verification. Restore exercises quarantine recovered authority and sessions. Neither a signature nor a backup proves present-day access closure.

03 / WHAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS

Useful claims
have edges.

A private controlled alpha, evaluated in a local laboratory. No production certification, external audit, universal identity-provider support, or enterprise-scale performance claim.

Demonstrated in the laboratory

  • One Keycloak realm and one controlled OIDC application.
  • A still-valid token accepted after its account was disabled.
  • Resource-side denial with a successful positive control.
  • Residual access, outage, and fresh recovery observations.
  • Historical signature verification, signing-key rotation, and encrypted recovery exercises.
  • Separate tests for concurrency, authorization boundaries, and bounded state transitions.

Still requires real-world validation

  • Application-specific session and token semantics.
  • Independent production adapters and customer environments.
  • Operational performance, failure modes, and support commitments at scale.
  • Independent review of the security model and implementation.
  • Organizational procedures, approval ownership, and legal compliance.
  • Commercial readiness beyond a controlled evaluation.

FREE TERMINAL EDITION / PUBLIC ALPHA

Run the check.
Keep the evidence.

Access Assurance Lite is a separate MIT-licensed tool. Python 3.11+, local operation, no account or cloud service. Start with the included HTTP laboratory, then connect a cooperating application.

Included in Lite

  • Original-credential baseline and paired positive controls.
  • Up to 16 configured resources and repeated observations.
  • Residual access, explicit policy denial and unknown outcomes.
  • Historical JSON evidence, CSV export and comparison.
  • Runnable local demo and a synthetic correctness benchmark.

Separate private commercial candidate

  • Team and site authorization with approval roles.
  • Bounded intervention planning and durable execution.
  • Signed history, key rotation and controlled recovery.
  • Broader deployments and commercial support still require productization.
Download Lite and run the local demonstration→

Lite uses a cooperating-resource protocol and hash-based historical evidence. It does not include administrative actions or signed private receipts. The private Keycloak evaluation above and Lite's synthetic HTTP demo are different evaluations.
